title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: conversation orchestration with natural language playbooks
summary: The briefing largely matches Microsoft's documentation and rollout notice. However, its automation column supplies a read-only list request for a control that changes queue scope and publishes playbooks; administrators cannot use that request to perform those actions. The discussion of switches should also acknowledge Microsoft's documented feature toggle.

claims.claim: Copilot credits are consumed when a playbook is published.
claims.quote: Conversation orchestration consumes Copilot credits only when you publish a playbook, which makes the configured orchestration logic active for use.
claims.fix: Add: 'The overflow documentation also describes a planned credit exemption for upgrades and for playbooks with one branch containing only the wait-time-in-queue-exceeds condition and no context variables.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/customer-service/administer/manage-overflow#upgrade-legacy-in-queue-overflow-to-a-conversation-orchestration-playbook. That page says: 'Under the planned credit exemption, upgrading a single queue or multiple queues doesn't use Copilot credits.' It also exempts qualifying upgraded and newly created playbooks. Keep the general feature-page statement attributed rather than implying every publish necessarily incurs a charge.
